format: gfm

## Layers

```text
PySide6 GUI
  └─ controllers and background workers
       └─ Digitizer / Scope / MCA / HV interfaces
            ├─ IIO backend (current)
            │    └─ libiio → iiod → FPGA and converter IIO devices
            └─ gRPC backend (legacy)
                 └─ Engine/IDS gRPC + ZMQ DMA services

External workspace
  └─ nlab-modbus → Modbus TCP / ser2net → RS-485 instruments
```

High-level hardware interfaces are shared across backends. DMA implementations
are intentionally backend-specific because the current IIO buffer lifecycle is
not interchangeable with the legacy server-pushed ZMQ streams.

## Context and thread ownership

One libiio context is not shared across GUI control, polling, viewer, and
blocking DMA threads. Each background activity owns its context and device
handles. This prevents a blocking refill from serializing unrelated control
writes on the same remote connection.

| Activity | Owner |
|---|---|
| GUI settings and direct reads | Controller-side `Digitizer` backend |
| Scope live viewer | Isolated Scope client |
| IIR current polling | Worker-owned current-monitor client |
| Scope DMA refill | Scope DMA worker/backend capture context |
| MCA list-mode refill | MCA DMA worker/backend capture context |
| File output | Dedicated bounded writer queue/thread where applicable |

Exceptions crossing a thread boundary are reduced to scalar error data. Keeping
native exception tracebacks can retain IIO buffers and delay hardware-gate
cleanup.

## Scope DMA lifecycle

The required order is:

1. stop the acquisition core;
2. configure scan elements and validate driver-advertised geometry;
3. create the buffer and start the first blocking refill on the DMA thread;
4. enable acquisition only after that reader is waiting;
5. accept complete frames only;
6. stop the core before drain/close;
7. cancel or drain the reader, join its thread, explicitly destroy the native
   buffer, and wait for ownership gates to clear.

Buffer callbacks own the DMA gate; application code must not write
`dma_enable` directly. Persistent `EINVAL` or `EIO` ends and latches the
session. Recovery acknowledgement is required before rearming instead of
recreating buffers mid-file.

Current firmware can advertise four queued Scope kernel blocks. Qualified
remote capture uses READBUF batches of 64 frames to amortize network round
trips while preserving exact hardware frame boundaries. Firmware without the
queue capability remains on the conservative one-block path.

## MCA DMA lifecycle

Current list mode transports complete 16 KiB blocks of 1,024 opaque records.
The first reader is armed before the pulse processor starts. Stop gates event
production, then the reader drains complete tail blocks before destroying the
buffer. Reconfiguration is forbidden while list DMA owns the pulse processor.

File output uses bounded queues. Storage that remains slower than acquisition
causes explicit backpressure or failure; it must never silently drop records
and leave a capture looking complete.

## Current-monitor data flow

IIR mode polls one signed filter register into a bounded sample buffer. The GUI
drains it at a capped display cadence and retains a ten-second history.

Scope Current DMA validates every record and updates exact signed sums/sample
counts on the receiver thread. Only after scientific accumulation does it
publish replaceable preview data. Scalar rendering and waveform painting have
separate cadence limits, so skipped GUI generations do not imply skipped
scientific observations.

## MCA snapshots

Histogram and debug data can be exposed as split or monolithic binary
attributes depending on firmware. Large remote attributes may have one verified
transport terminator; only that final NUL is removed because embedded zero
bytes are valid. Multi-chunk histogram reads are sequential and not atomic
while acquisition runs.

## Device discovery

Pulse-processor and list-mode devices use `channel_index` for stable pairing.
Scope and input-filter discovery may use sorted `iio:deviceN` order as a
compatibility fallback. Sorting is deterministic but does not establish the
physical channel; validate mapping after target changes.

| `src/nlab/hardware/digitizer/backends/iio_ids_backend.py` | IDS/HV and global diagnostics |

| `src/nlab/workers/` | Polling, DMA, analysis, and device workers |
| `src/nlab/controllers/` | GUI state, ownership, and coordination |
| `src/nlab/analysis/` | Bounded offline readers and analysis models |

## Source of truth

Driver registers, units, ranges, scan layouts, and lifecycle rules come from
the corresponding PetaLinux repository revision. IIO sysfs attributes normally
already contain the user/physical value after kernel conversion. Only explicit
`*_raw` plus `*_scale` pairs require caller-side scaling.

A get-after-set round trip cannot detect a symmetric double conversion. Changes
must be checked against driver encoding and range boundaries. Live hardware
results, source-derived behavior, and simulated/unit-tested behavior should be
labelled separately.
